extracted.intended_audience: federal agency procurement officers, ADP planners, and contracting officials (GSA/OMB reporting officials)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for preparing agency-wide Automatic Data Processing (ADP) plans, specifying what supplemental information must accompany OMB A-11 submissions, and for procurement/specification of ADP items and services including interactions with contractors and GSA. Intended to ensure efficient, economic, and competitive ADP acquisition and management across federal agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual ADP plan submission (OMB Circular A-11) and concurrent GSA copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to prepare and submit annual agency-wide ADP plans in accordance with OMB Circular A-11. A copy of this plan shall be provided to GSA (CPS) concurrently with each submission to OMB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The information will be used by GSA in compiling Government-wide requirements and developing acquisition programs to assist agencies in meeting their needs in an efficient and economic manner. The page also instructs forwarding the GSA copy of the submission to the named ADP Planning and Authorization Branch contact (Ms. I. S. Bayol) to assist in orderly receipt and control of submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental information — trends in data processing workloads
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit trends in data processing workloads that will or may saturate existing ADP system capabilities prior to expiration of the full established initial user's system/item(s) life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to identify near-term capacity shortfalls so GSA and agencies can plan acquisitions and avoid system saturation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental information — opportunities from new technology and market changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit opportunities to take advantage of cost effective enhancements brought about by new ADPE technology, software improvements, and changes in the marketplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information should highlight potential cost-saving or performance-improving upgrades and market-driven alternatives that could affect acquisition strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental information — planned system redesign and software actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit actions planned regarding system redesign to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of application software, the conversion of software to higher level languages, and the audit and update of documentation for consistency with the guidelines issued by the National Bureau of Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers planned software modernization, language conversion, and documentation updates; links to standards/guidelines (National Bureau of Standards) for documentation consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental information — approximate acquisition schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit an approximate acquisition schedule with the ADP plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides timeline context for planned procurements to support Government-wide program planning and coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental information — proposed acquisition strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit the proposed acquisition strategy for meeting projected ADP resource needs identified in the ADP plans submitted pursuant to OMB Circular A-11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should describe how the agency intends to procure resources (e.g., severing, GFE, purchase vs lease) to meet projected needs efficiently and economically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement applicable FED-STD and comply with waiver/exception procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart 101-35.2 MANAGEMENT, ACQUISITION, AND UTILIZATION OF AUTOMATIC DATA PROCESSING (ADP) (FED-STD) shall be implemented when applicable. Procedures for waiver or exception shall be complied with for each applicable mandatory FIPS PUB or FED-STD that is not implemented (see Subpart 101-36.13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where mandatory Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) or Federal Standards (FED-STD) apply, agencies must implement them or follow formal waiver/exception procedures; cross-reference to Subpart 101-36.13 for waiver procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability when ADP incorporated into non-ADP contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: When the very subject matter of a contract is for something other than the procurement of ADP items or services and commercially available ADPE is incorporated into the non-ADP system or commercial ADP services are used in contract performance, the acquisition and management of the non-ADP system shall be in accordance with other applicable regulations, rather than this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes procurement/management jurisdiction when ADP components are incidental to a non-ADP contract; use other applicable regulations in those cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor identification of ADPE delivered with non-ADP systems
rubrics_metrics.description: To facilitate the reutilization of ADPE, the Government contractor shall be required to identify the quantity and specific make and model of the ADPE that is delivered as a part of the non-ADP system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identification supports reutilization and asset management; it is a contractor reporting requirement when ADPE is supplied as part of a larger non-ADP deliverable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sever general-purpose commercially available ADP items/services and provide as GFE when feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall sever requirements for general purpose commercially available ADP items or services from the overall requirement, acquire them in accordance with these regulations, and provide them as Government-furnished property or services to the contractor when it is operationally feasible to do so and this action will promote economy, efficiency, and maximum practicable competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy favors separating commoditized ADP elements from contractor-procured work so government can centrally procure/provide them to promote competition, efficiency, and economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect prime contractor performance when Government procures severed ADP items/services
rubrics_metrics.description: In those instances when ADP items or services are severed pursuant to this subpart and procured by the Government, care must be taken to ensure that the prime contractor's ability and responsibility to perform in accordance with the contract provisions are not disturbed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the government takes over procurement of severed ADP elements, it must manage transitions so the prime contractor can still meet contractual obligations without performance disruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design specifications to promote maximum practicable competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifications and purchase descriptions describing Government requirements shall be designed to promote competition to the maximum practicable extent from manufacturers, leasing companies, third-party vendors, and ADP services contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes competitive sourcing across suppliers and service providers; drafting of requirements should avoid unnecessary vendor lock-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer functional specifications; augment with equipment/performance criteria as necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional specifications maximize competition and are the preferred method for expressing the user's requirements. Functional specifications may be augmented with equipment characteristics and performance criteria as necessary to accurately reflect the user's needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use functional (requirements-focused) specs to maximize competition; where necessary, add specific equipment or performance criteria to ensure the requirement is met. References to FPR sections (e.g., 1-4.1102-12, 1-4.1109-10, 1-4.1109-11) are provided for further procedural detail.
